sections.history: Thalaichangadu, near Akkur in the Mayiladuthurai country of the Kaveri delta, holds Thalaichanga Nanmathiyam, one of the 108 Divya Desams — the abodes of Vishnu sung by the Alvar saints in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham — and part of Chola Nadu. Its mangalasasanam was offered by Thirumangai Alvar, the last great poet of the Alvar tradition. The presiding lord is Nanmathiya Perumal, with Thalaichanga Nachiyar, and the festival image is worshipped as Vensudar Perumal. The shrine's standing rests on the Alvar's hymns and the long devotion of the village. In the same village stands the Sangaranyeswarar shrine of Shiva, a separate temple praised in the Thevaram.
sections.architecture: The temple follows the Dravidian plan of the Chola country: a single-tiered gopuram marks the entrance, and the sanctum holds Nanmathiya Perumal standing and facing east. Tradition describes a crescent moon on the lord's head, the sign by which he is known. The Goddess has her own shrine as Thalaichanga Nachiyar, and the Chandra Pushkarini, the temple tank, lies in front of the temple.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells of Chandra, the Moon, who was cursed by his guru Brihaspati to a wasting sickness. Seeking release, he and the devas worshipped Vishnu in this place, and the lord relieved him of the curse — hence the epithet Chandra Shaba Harar, and the tank that bears the Moon's name. The village name is also explained in tradition by the conch, sangu, and by an association with the first Tamil Sangam.
sections.festivals: The temple observes the Vaishnava calendar, above all Vaikunta Ekadashi, and keeps the days of Thirumangai Alvar, the poet-saint who sang this shrine. Local priests can say which are celebrated and when.
sections.experience: A quiet village shrine among the paddy fields, free of crowds. Stand before the east-facing lord, walk down to the Chandra Pushkarini, and pair the visit with the other Divya Desams near Sirkazhi, such as Thiruvali-Thirunagari and the Thirunangur group.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Thalaichangadu lies in the Kaveri delta of Mayiladuthurai district, near Akkur, and is reached by road from Sirkazhi or Mayiladuthurai. The nearest railheads are Sirkazhi and Mayiladuthurai on the Chennai line; the nearest major airport is Tiruchirappalli, about 160 km away.
